  - A 1910 meeting at Jekyll Island helped draft a proposal (the Aldrich Plan). Participants included Sen. Nelson Aldrich, Frank Vanderlip (National City Bank), Henry P. Davison (J.P. Morgan & Co.), Paul Warburg (Kuhn, Loeb & Co.), Benjamin Strong (Bankers Trust), and A. Piatt Andrew. No reliable historical account places any Rothschild family member there or directing the effort.
    - Source: Federal Reserve History (Jekyll Island): https://www.federalreservehistory.org/essays/jekyll-island

- How the Federal Reserve is governed
  - The Fed has a public–private structure, but its policy decisions are made by public officials. The Board of Governors (in Washington, D.C.) is a federal agency; its members are nominated by the U.S. President and confirmed by the Senate. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) includes the Board and Reserve Bank presidents.
    - Source: Federal Reserve: https://www.federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/structure-federal-reserve-system.htm
  - Reserve Banks issue non‑transferable stock to member banks; this does not confer control like a typical corporation (dividends are capped by law, and policy is not set by shareholders).
    - Source: Federal Reserve FAQ “Who owns the Fed?”: https://www.federalreserve.gov/faqs/about_14986.htm
  - The Fed’s financial statements are audited annually by an external auditor, and many functions are subject to Government Accountability Office (GAO) review.
    - Source: Federal Reserve FAQ “Is the Fed audited?”: https://www.federalreserve.gov/faqs/about_12784.htm

- About the Rothschild family

      - Encyclopaedia Britannica (Rothschild family): https://www.britannica.com/topic/Rothschild-family

  - The global financial system is decentralized:

Why the restriction was added
- Congressional concern about advocacy: The original 1996 Dickey Amendment for CDC, and the 2011 NIH rider, were enacted by members of Congress who argued federal health agencies had used research funds in ways that looked like policy advocacy for gun control.
